research_question: Can Q.ANT-style training noise improve the robustness of a fixed QFourier g4 model to the toolkit's periodic Q.ANT evaluation, reducing reference-to-Q.ANT disagreement without sacrificing useful Fashion-MNIST accuracy?
observations: Exp011 found qfourier_g4 to be the strongest tested Fourier capacity point: mean Q.ANT accuracy 0.82987 with 62,730 parameters.
Increasing capacity further to g8 reduced mean Q.ANT accuracy to 0.82103 and increased mean prediction disagreement to about 586.7 of 10,000.
For g4, mean prediction disagreement remained high at 323 of 10,000 compared with about 6.7 for the h64_512 ReLU control.
Q.ANT's official QFourier example supports injected training noise; Exp010 and Exp011 intentionally used no training noise.
hypothesis: For a locked QFourier g4 architecture, training with Q.ANT-style Gaussian noise will reduce reference-to-Q.ANT prediction disagreement relative to the no-noise baseline while preserving or improving mean Q.ANT-backend accuracy.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if neither pre-registered noise condition reduces mean prediction disagreement relative to the no-noise g4 baseline, or if any disagreement reduction is accompanied by a material loss of mean Q.ANT accuracy that removes the model's useful accuracy-versus-parameter trade-off.

proposed_method.training_rule: During training, add zero-mean Gaussian noise with the pre-registered standard deviation to the exact-cosine Fourier response, following the robustness mechanism exposed by Q.ANT's QFourier example. Evaluate every trained model both with the exact PyTorch reference and qant.ai.calc_kan_layer_fprop.

limitations: Q.ANT CPU backend only; this does not measure photonic hardware performance.
The experiment tests training noise as a robustness intervention; it does not prove the same optimum will hold on physical Q.ANT hardware.
Fashion-MNIST, three seeds, and three epochs limit precision and generality.
Noise levels are locked before execution to avoid post-hoc tuning.
